Bèta in Bestuur & Beleid carrièredag | 25 november 2026
Event
-
25 November 2026
Op 25 november 2026 organiseert Bèta in Bestuur & Beleid (BiBB) een carrièredag in Sociëteit De Witte in Den Haag. De dag is relevant voor promovendi, postdocs en masterstudenten met een bèta- of technische achtergrond die zich oriënteren op een mogelijke loopbaan in beleid, bestuur of politiek.
Veel bèta’s zien beleid, bestuur of politiek niet direct als een logische carrièreroute. Tegelijkertijd zijn juist zij, door hun analytisch vermogen, inhoudelijke diepgang en ervaring met complexe vraagstukken, goed toegerust om bij te dragen aan maatschappelijke thema’s rond bijvoorbeeld klimaat, energie, digitalisering, gezondheid en veiligheid.
Tijdens de BiBB Carrièredag krijgen deelnemers concrete handvatten om een stap richting bestuur, beleid of politiek te verkennen. Het programma bestaat uit lezingen, workshops, een carrièremarkt en gesprekken met professionals uit het veld. Ook zijn er sprekers zoals Henri Bontenbal en Jan Anthonie Bruijn, voormalig minister van VWS.
Datum: 25 november
Locatie: Sociëteit De Witte, Den Haag
Doelgroep: promovendi, postdocs en masterstudenten met een bèta- of technische achtergrond
Tickets: https://www.betainbestuurenbeleid.nl/carrièredag

Meet the newest member of PE&RC!
PE&RC Office
-
26 October 2026
We are delighted to welcome our new colleague to PE&RC as a PhD Programme Coordinator, Mathilde Janssen! With a background in Chemistry and previous experience as a Programme Coordinator at NWO, she brings valuable experience and a passion for supporting PhD candidates and helping students grow as scientists. In this introduction, get to know her a little better. Welcome to the PE&RC community!
Mathilde: As of October, I have joined PE&RC as a PhD Programme Coordinator. After completing my PhD, I spent two years working as a Programme Coordinator at NWO, and I’m very happy to be back in an academic environment. Outside of work, I love staying active. My volleyball, cycling, running, walking, and climbing shoes all get regular use. I also enjoy cooking, reading, and playing board games. And if there’s any time left over, I like to get behind the sewing machine.
What are you passionate about in your research?
I completed my PhD in Chemistry in 2024, but while I was still a PhD candidate, I was most passionate about sharing my knowledge with bachelor’s and master’s students. I enjoyed seeing them grow more confident as scientists and working together on my research projects. During my PhD, I supervised 13 students over four years, sometimes as many as three at a time.
What is your favourite book? / What is a good/bad book you've read recently?
I love a good thriller, and one of my recent favourites was the Scandinavian novel The Chestnut Man by Søren Sveistrup. I’ve been told there’s also a Netflix series based on the book, although I haven’t watched it yet. To be honest, I’m not very good at watching thrillers, they're usually a bit too scary for me!
If you do not enjoy a thriller, I would also recommend I Who Have Never Known Men. It’s unlike anything I’ve ever read. It’s difficult to describe what it’s about without giving too much away, so I would simply say: give it a try!
If you could have any superpower, what would you choose, and why?
I wish I could travel anywhere instantly. I’d love to be able to visit my family in the south of the Netherlands for a coffee and a vlaai without spending two hours on the train. It would also make it much easier to visit friends who are doing postdocs abroad, spend time with my partner’s family in the UK, and, of course, see my partner more often, since he lives in The Hague.
What is something that instantly makes your day better?
I’m very easily satisfied. My day instantly gets better when I spot a double rainbow, when dinner is already cooked when I get home, or when I unexpectedly run into friends.
What is your useless talent?
My useless talent is that I’m surprisingly good at fast walking!
I’m really excited to be part of the PE&RC community and look forward to meeting many of you during courses, events, and other activities. If you have any questions about PhD courses, training requirements, or anything else related to the graduate programme, please don’t hesitate to get in touch. I’m always happy to help!

Whether it’s a publication, media appearance, conference presentation, research milestone, award, outreach activity, or something else you’re proud of, get in touch and tell us about it. PPC interview with....
PPC
-
28 June 2026
What is your PhD topic?
My PhD topic is to analyse European forest regrowth rates. For this we use repeated national forest inventory data that many European countries have been collecting over the last decades. We compare how much carbon the forests had stored in the past and how this changes in following measurements over the next years and decades. From this we can assess the regrowth rates of different forests.
These rates are then useful for all kind of carbon accounting models and to inform management and climate policy.
When you applied for this job, what interested you the most about the PhD topic?
During my master’s, and as a project assistant after my master’s, I did global mechanistic vegetation modelling. And while I like that a lot, you don't actually see what’s happening on the ground or what the forests look like. I think it was crucial for me to find a PhD that included fieldwork and would allow me to work more directly with real data, while also complementing my background of global or big pattern thinking. Therefore this position worked quite well for me.
What is your favourite thing about the research groups you work in?
In FEM I like the scientific exchange and the international bubble. In SFE I like the general support for research ideas, generally in whatever direction I want to investigate.
What is something that you would like to contribute to these groups?
At FEM, everyone loves to study tropical forests. I'm trying to keep people interested in the forest around us instead of always looking overseas into these, you know, warm regions. On the SFE side, I like to bring knowledge on mechanistic modelling and big data management, as we work in a field with growing datasets. I think the group is generally quite appreciative of this.
How has this project so far influenced or changed you as a person or maybe your goals or future interests?
As a master student, you mostly work on your own on a little problem. Sure, you talk to your supervisors, but it's not really integrated into a bigger context. Now, for my PhD, there is a large network. I’ve visited research groups in Munich, in Oslo and Umeå. We can link our ideas and see how our research interests can combine into a larger project. I appreciate that a lot.
